name: 独耳掌
One-Ear's Forge
before: 野地上，一伙牧主家的牦牛骑正围着一个独耳朵的老头打，说他偷马。老头确实偷马，可偷的都是掌钉得歪七扭八的马，牵回窝里重钉一副好掌，第二天夜里再悄悄送回去。失主们早上起来一看，马走得比原先还稳，又气又说不出话。

Out in the open a troop of a herd-owner's yak riders is beating an old man with one ear, calling him a horse thief. He does steal horses, it's true, but only ones with badly set shoes. He leads them home, shoes them properly, and sneaks them back the next night. Their owners wake up to horses walking better than before, and don't know whether to be angry.
after: 牦牛骑被打散了。独耳是碎石营当年的掌钉匠，营将关那汉人的那几天，是他去送的饭。他说那汉人从匣里取出半张纸给营将看，密密麻麻全是名字：「后头还有人要过这座山。你封了山，他们就死在山下。」营将看了一夜，第二天就开了马厩。

The riders are scattered. One-Ear was the Gravel Camp's farrier, and it was he who took the locked-up Han man his meals. The man took half a sheet of paper from his casket and showed it to the commander, he says, covered in names: 'There are more coming over this mountain behind me. Close it, and they'll die at its foot.' The commander studied it all night, and next morning opened the stable door.

name: 试山棍
The Testing Staves
before: 碎石滩上，一队护法僧兵拦着一支想过山的驮队，一个个比试过去：赢一个，过一个；输了的，掉头回去。驮队的人骂他们欺负人，僧兵也不辩，只把包铁的长棍往碎石里一戳。轮到你们，领头的僧兵把棍子横了过来。

On the gravel flats a squad of temple warrior-monks has stopped a pack train that wants to cross the mountain, and is testing them one by one: beat a monk and you pass; lose and you turn back. The pack men curse them for bullies, and the monks don't argue, only plant their iron-capped staves in the gravel. When your turn comes, the leading monk turns his staff crosswise.
after: 僧兵们收了棍，放驮队和你们一起过去。领头的说，「冬不过山」不是不让过，是要打得过他们才能过：「打不过我们的，过了垭口也是冻死。」这规矩是山神九年前定的，原本是一道封山的旨意，山神把它改成了一场比试：「封山，封的是送死的人。」

The monks lower their staves and let the pack train through with you. 'No crossing in winter' doesn't mean no one crosses, their leader says. It means you must beat them first: 'Anyone who can't beat us would freeze to death on the col anyway.' The Mountain God made the rule nine years ago. It began as an edict closing the mountain, and the god turned it into a trial: 'We close the mountain only to those who'd die on it.'

name: 雪崩口
Avalanche Mouth
before: 转山道在山脚被一场新雪崩截断了。一伙「路把头」抢先在雪里挖出一条窄道，守在两头收钱，一个人一块银子，不给的就从雪崩堆上爬。阿旺转到了第十三圈，趴在雪堆前，额头磕得出了血，他们还在一旁笑，看他怎么爬过去。

The pilgrim circuit at the mountain's foot has been cut by a fresh avalanche. A gang of 'road bosses' got there first and dug a narrow passage through the snow, and now they stand at both ends charging a lump of silver a head; anyone who won't pay can climb over the debris. Awang is on his thirteenth circuit, prostrate before the snow, his forehead bleeding, while they stand by laughing to see how he'll get over.
after: 路把头被赶走了，窄道白给人走。阿旺坐在雪堆上喘气，这才说出来：他是碎石营的逃兵。十年前擂「撤营」那夜，他第一个跑了，后来才听说营将没走，一个人留了下来。「我跑了，营将没跑。」他擦掉额头的血，「这十三圈，是替营将转的。」

The road bosses are driven off, and the passage is free to all. Awang sits on the snow heap to catch his breath, and at last tells you: he deserted from the Gravel Camp. The night the drum beat 'Strike camp' ten years ago he was the first to run, and only heard later that the commander hadn't gone, but stayed behind alone. 'I ran. The commander didn't.' He wipes the blood from his forehead. 'These thirteen circuits are for him.'

name: 孤烽墩
The Lone Beacon
before: 碎石滩上一座孤零零的烽墩，是碎石营的旧烽火台。一伙盐枭的弓手蹲在墩顶放哨，替私盐驮队望风，看见远处有人就放一支响箭。墩底下压着一摞烽火簿，被他们撕了引火，烧得只剩最后几页。

A lone beacon tower stands on the gravel flats, the Gravel Camp's old signal post. A band of the salt smugglers' archers squats on top keeping watch for the contraband trains, loosing a whistling arrow whenever someone shows on the horizon. Under the tower lies a pile of beacon logs, torn up for kindling, burned down to the last few pages.
after: 弓手被赶下了墩。烧剩的最后一页写着：「撤营之日，烽不举。次夜，营将亲举一烽，向山。」老兵们说，那是给雪山上的庙报信：有人要上山，下来接。那一夜，山上果然亮起一盏灯，亮了很久。

The archers are driven down from the tower. The last surviving page reads: 'Day of striking camp: no beacon lit. Next night: one beacon, towards the mountain, lit by the commander himself.' That was a message to the temple on the snow mountain, the old soldiers say: someone is coming up, come down to meet him. And that night, sure enough, a lamp shone on the mountain, for a long time.

name: 碎石营
Gravel Camp
before: 山脚下一圈石墙，墙是拿碎石滩上的石头垒的，这就是碎石营。营门大开，一伙盗马贼在营里安了家，营将的大帐成了他们头领的马圈。几个跟着你们来的老兵站在营门口，谁也不肯先进去，像是怕营里有人点名。

A ring of stone walls stands at the mountain's foot, built of stones from the gravel flats: this is the Gravel Camp. Its gate stands open and a band of horse thieves has made it home; the commander's great tent is now their leader's horse pen. The old soldiers who have come with you stand at the gate, and none of them will go in first, as if afraid someone inside might call the roll.
after: 盗马贼被赶了出去。大帐里一个空甲架还立着，架下的地扫得干干净净，像是每个月都有人来扫。营簿最后一页是营将的字：「营将霍山，去甲。营可撤，人不走。」老兵们挨个在营簿上按了手印，按完了，才敢在帐里坐下。

The horse thieves are thrown out. In the great tent an empty armour stand still stands, and the ground beneath it is swept clean, as if someone comes every month to sweep it. The last page of the camp book is in the commander's hand: 'Commander Huo Shan lays down his armour. The camp may be struck. The man stays.' The old soldiers press their thumbprints in the book one by one, and only then dare to sit down in the tent.

name: 屯田坝
The Barley Terraces
before: 野地里一片青稞地，是碎石营当年屯的田，营散了，地还在，种地的是些兵的家眷，十年没走。一个外来的地头带着打手占了打谷场，说地是无主的，收的青稞一半归他，不给就烧场。一个头发花白的妇人举着连枷挡在谷堆前，一声不吭。

Out in the open lies a field of highland barley, the Gravel Camp's old military farm. The camp is gone but the fields remain, worked by soldiers' families who never left in ten years. An outsider with a gang of bullies has taken the threshing floor, claiming the land has no owner and half the harvest is his, or he'll burn it. A grey-haired woman stands before the grain with a flail raised, saying nothing.
after: 打手们被赶走，打谷场上又响起了连枷声。花白头发的妇人说，每年秋收，都有个放牦牛的老汉来帮着割青稞，一句话不说，割完就走，「割得比谁都快，那架势，像在打仗」。她说完低头扎麦捆，扎得极紧，像是不想再多说。

The bullies are driven off and the flails ring on the threshing floor again. The grey-haired woman says that every harvest an old yak herder comes to help with the reaping. He never says a word and leaves when it's done. 'He reaps faster than anyone. Like a man in a battle.' Then she bends to tie sheaves, very tight, as if she'd rather not say more.
first: 地头的仓里抄出青稞六十袋、一架抢来的水磨盘、三口酥油坛、一串打手们赌输了押下的银耳环，还有一张写着「无主地」的假地契，妇人们拿它糊了窗户。

From the bully's store you take sixty sacks of barley, a stolen millstone, three crocks of butter, a string of silver earrings his men lost at dice, and a forged deed calling the land ownerless. The women use it to paper a window.
pass: 每次路过，屯田坝的妇人们都在你们车上放一袋新炒的青稞，炒得噼啪响，花白头发的那位总要多塞一把：「当兵的走远路，嚼着这个不饿。」

Every time you pass, the women of the terraces put a sack of freshly roasted barley on your cart, still crackling, and the grey-haired one always adds an extra handful: 'Soldiers on a long road. Chew on that and you won't go hungry.'

name: 甲匠窑
The Armourer's Kiln
before: 野地里一座窑洞，窑里叮叮当当打了十年皮甲，打甲的老匠人原是碎石营的。一伙穿红袍的假僧兵把他扣在窑里，逼他赶制三十副铁叶甲，好扮成神庙护法去吓唬过路人。老匠人一边打一边故意把甲叶穿反，被他们发现了，正挨鞭子。

Out in the open is a kiln-cave where hammers have rung on leather armour for ten years, and the old armourer who works it came from the Gravel Camp. A gang of false monks in red robes holds him there, demanding thirty suits of iron lamellar so they can pass as temple guardians and frighten travellers. He has been lacing the plates in backwards on purpose; they've caught him, and he is being whipped.
after: 假僧兵被打散，穿反的甲扔了一地。老匠人抹了把脸说，营将那副明光甲就是他打的，甲叶七百片，胸前一面护心镜。「营将交了甲，没交给朝廷，挂进了碎石滩上的山神祠。」他说营将的原话是：「甲是朝廷的，人是这座山的。」

The false monks are scattered, and the backwards armour lies all over the floor. The old armourer wipes his face. He made the commander's own armour, he says, seven hundred plates and a mirror over the heart. 'The commander laid it down, but not to the court. He hung it in the Mountain God's shrine on the gravel flats.' His words were: 'The armour belongs to the court. The man belongs to this mountain.'

name: 赏金帐
Bounty Tent
before: 野地上一顶大帐，帐前插着一面「捕」字旗，一伙骑牦牛的赏金客在这里落脚，挨个盘问过路的牧人，拿一张发黄的画像给人认。画像上是个年轻的将军，浓眉，披着明光甲。谁说没见过，他们就扣下谁的一头牛，说是「问话钱」。

A big tent stands in the open with a CAPTURE flag planted before it. A band of bounty hunters on yaks has set up here, stopping every passing herder to show him a yellowed portrait: a young general with heavy brows in bright plate armour. Anyone who says he hasn't seen him loses a yak, as a 'questioning fee'.
after: 赏金客被打出了帐，扣下的牛还了回去。画像背面是十年前的海捕文书：「碎石营营将霍山，抗旨纵人过山，弃甲潜逃。赏银三百两。」老兵们看着画像，说营将年轻时就是这个样子，如今要是还活着，谁也认不出了。

The bounty hunters are driven out and the seized yaks returned. On the back of the portrait is a ten-year-old warrant: 'Huo Shan, commander of the Gravel Camp, defied the edict and let a man over the mountain, then abandoned his armour and fled. Reward three hundred taels.' The old soldiers look at the portrait. That's how the commander looked when he was young, they say. If he's still alive, no one would know him now.

name: 交牌垭
Token Col
before: 转山道的最高处是一道垭口，垭口上一座玛尼堆，比人还高，每块石头上都刻着经文。这是阿旺第十三圈的终点。一伙盗马贼里最狠的人马占了垭口，专扒玛尼堆里供着的银子和珊瑚，刀、弓、马排了三层。阿旺不看他们，只盯着那堆石头，攥紧了怀里一样东西。

The highest point of the pilgrim circuit is a col, crowned by a mani cairn taller than a man, every stone carved with scripture. This is where Awang's thirteenth circuit ends. The hardest men among the horse thieves hold the col, stripping the silver and coral offerings from the cairn, three ranks deep of blades, bows and horses. Awang doesn't look at them. He watches the cairn, gripping something inside his coat.
after:
盗马贼被打下了垭口。阿旺从怀里掏出一块磨亮的木腰牌，碎石营的兵牌，压进玛尼堆里。手一伸进去，碰到的全是牌：几十块碎石营的兵牌，一块压着一块，都是这些年逃了又回来的人放的。最上面一块石头刻着一行小字：「回来的，都还是碎石营的兵。霍。」刻痕是新的。

阿旺跪在那里，把那片十年的茶叶放进嘴里嚼了很久，说：「是甜的。」

The horse thieves are driven off the col. Awang takes a worn wooden tag from his coat, a Gravel Camp soldier's tag, and pushes it into the cairn. His hand meets nothing but tags: dozens of Gravel Camp tags, one on another, left over the years by men who ran and came back. On the topmost stone a line has been carved: 'Those who come back are still soldiers of the Gravel Camp. Huo.' The cuts are fresh.

Awang kneels there, puts the ten-year-old tea leaf in his mouth, and chews it a long time. 'It's sweet,' he says.

name: 牛蹄印
Yak Tracks
before: 野地的雪上有一行牦牛蹄印，一头牛，一个人，往碎石滩深处去。几个赏金客骑着牦牛顺着蹄印追，追到一个放牛娃的帐篷，把娃娃吊起来问话：那头牦牛的主人是谁，住在哪儿。娃娃咬着牙，一个字也不说。

A line of yak tracks crosses the snow, one yak and one man, heading deep into the gravel flats. Some bounty hunters on yaks are following them, and the tracks have brought them to a herd boy's tent. They've hung the boy up to question him: who owns that yak, where does he live? The boy grits his teeth and says nothing.
after: 赏金客被打跑，娃娃被放了下来，揉着手腕说，那是他东家，一个放牦牛的老汉，从不说自己叫什么，大伙都叫他「老石头」。「老石头说，谁来问，都说没见过。」娃娃想了想又说：「他左手少一根指头，挤奶比谁都快。」

The bounty hunters are chased off and the boy let down. Rubbing his wrists, he says it's his master, an old yak herder who never says his name; everyone calls him Old Stone. 'Old Stone said, whoever asks, say you haven't seen him.' He thinks, then adds: 'He's got a finger missing on his left hand. Milks faster than anyone though.'

name: 副将帐
The Lieutenant's Camp
before: 碎石滩上一伙牦牛骑扎了营，领头的是个满脸刀疤的中年汉子，自称碎石营的副将。他恨营将恨了十年：营将抗了旨，碎石营五百人一个也没落着好，散的散，抓的抓，他自己挨了八十军棍。这回他带人来，就是要亲手把营将拿回去。

A troop of yak riders has camped on the gravel flats, led by a middle-aged man with a face full of sword scars who calls himself the Gravel Camp's lieutenant. He has hated the commander for ten years: the commander defied the edict, and not one of the camp's five hundred came out of it well, scattered or arrested, and he himself got eighty strokes of the rod. He's here to drag the commander back with his own hands.
after: 牦牛骑散了，副将坐在雪地里不肯起来。老兵们把营簿、靶桩上的字、粮仓墙上的账一样样讲给他听。他听完半天没出声，最后说：「撤营的旨意早就下了，营怎么都得散。他放的那个人，是替我们守山去了？」他把刀插回了鞘里。

The riders scatter, and the lieutenant sits in the snow and won't get up. The old soldiers tell him everything, the camp book, the words on the target post, the accounts on the granary wall. He is silent a long while, then says: 'The edict to strike camp had come already. The camp was finished either way. And the man he let through went up to guard the mountain for us?' He puts his sword back in its sheath.

name: 归营坡
Muster Slope
before: 野地坡上，赏金客花钱雇来的一大帮人马排开了阵，刀手、弓手、牦牛骑，足有两三百，堵住了往碎石滩深处去的路。坡下，零零散散地站着你们一路遇见的碎石营老兵，有劫过道的，有守鼓的，有钉掌的，还有那个副将，谁也没穿甲，手里拿的是赶牛的棍子。

On an open slope a great force hired with the bounty hunters' silver is drawn up, swordsmen, archers and yak riders, two or three hundred strong, blocking the way deeper into the gravel flats. Below the slope, here and there, stand the Gravel Camp's old soldiers you have met along the road: the ones who robbed, the one who keeps the drum, the farrier, and the lieutenant too. None of them wears armour. They carry yak-driving sticks.
after: 雇来的人马被打散了。老兵们在坡上竖起那面「霍」字旗，副将一个个点名，点到谁，谁就喊一声「到」。有人点着点着哭了。副将说：「营将要是知道，我们又站齐了……」他没说完，只说要去碎石滩深处的山神祠，替营将守着那副甲。

The hired force is scattered. The old soldiers raise the Huo banner on the slope, and the lieutenant calls the roll, and each man answers 'Here!' as his name is called. Someone starts crying partway through. 'If the commander knew we'd stood together again...' says the lieutenant, and doesn't finish. He only says he's going to the Mountain God's shrine deep in the gravel flats, to guard the commander's armour.

name: 军医窑
The Surgeon's Cave
before: 野地尽头一孔土窑，窑口挂着草药，住着碎石营的老军医。一伙雪山弓手占了窑，逼他天天给他们的头领治冻伤，治不好就不给饭吃。头领的两只脚冻得发黑，老军医说得截，头领不肯，叫手下拿箭顶着老军医的后脑勺。

At the end of the open ground is an earth cave hung with herbs, where the Gravel Camp's old surgeon lives. A band of snow-mountain archers has taken it and makes him treat their leader's frostbite every day, no food if he fails. The leader's feet are black with it. The old surgeon says they must come off; the leader refuses, and has his men hold an arrow to the back of the surgeon's head.
after: 弓手被赶走，头领被抬下山去截脚了。老军医说他这辈子截过一根最舍不得的指头：那年腊月，营将送那个汉人到雪山脚下，在风雪里等山上的人下来接，等了一夜，回来时左手小指冻黑了。「我截的时候他一声没吭，只问那人上去了没有。」

The archers are driven off and their leader carried down the mountain to lose his feet. The old surgeon says the finger he was sorriest to take in all his life was one little finger. That twelfth month, the commander walked the Han man to the foot of the snow mountain and waited all night in the blizzard for the people from the mountain to come down for him. When he came back, the little finger of his left hand was black. 'He didn't make a sound while I cut. He only asked if the man had got up safely.'

name: 驿袋堆
The Mailbag Cairn
before: 碎石滩上一个石头堆，石缝里塞着一只发霉的驿袋，是十年前封山那年没送出去的军邮。一伙盗马贼在石堆边生火，从驿袋里一封封抽信出来引火，烧一封骂一句：「全是哭哭啼啼的。」火边只剩最后几封了。

On the gravel flats stands a cairn of stones with a mouldy mailbag stuffed into a crack: army post that never went out the year the mountain was closed. A band of horse thieves has lit a fire beside it and is pulling the letters out one by one for kindling, cursing as each one burns: 'All of them snivelling.' Only a few are left by the fire.
after: 盗马贼被赶跑，你们从火边抢下了最后三封。两封已经烧得看不清，第三封完好，封口压着碎石营的火漆，信封上写着：「寄凉州，霍门秦氏」。没有人敢拆。老兵们说，营里姓霍的，只有一个。

The horse thieves are chased off and you snatch the last three letters from the fire. Two are too burnt to read. The third is whole, sealed with the Gravel Camp's wax, and addressed: 'To Liangzhou, to Mistress Qin of the house of Huo.' No one dares open it. There was only one man in the camp named Huo, the old soldiers say.

name: 秦婶灶
Aunt Qin's Stove
before: 野地上一间土屋，屋主是屯田坝那个花白头发的妇人，大家叫她秦婶。几个赏金客把她堵在灶房里，说打听过了，她是霍山的老婆，十年前从凉州找来的，不说霍山在哪儿，就把她带回去顶罪。秦婶往灶里添了一把柴，说她找了十年，也想知道他在哪儿。

Out in the open stands a mud house belonging to the grey-haired woman from the barley terraces, whom everyone calls Aunt Qin. A few bounty hunters have her cornered in her kitchen: they've found out she is Huo Shan's wife, come from Liangzhou ten years ago to look for him, and if she won't say where he is, they'll take her back to answer for him. Aunt Qin feeds a stick into the stove and says she has been looking for ten years, and would like to know herself.
after: 赏金客被打跑了。秦婶说她十年前来时，人人都说营将逃了，有的说死在雪里了。她就在屯田坝住下种麦，「他要是活着，早该回家了。不回，就是有放不下的事」。你们没提那封信。她给你们一人盛了一碗面片，面煮得透透的，锅盖上压着一块平石头。

The bounty hunters are chased off. When she came ten years ago, Aunt Qin says, everyone said the commander had fled; some said he died in the snow. So she stayed on the terraces and farmed barley. 'If he were alive he'd have come home long ago. If he hasn't, there's something he can't put down.' You don't mention the letter. She serves you each a bowl of noodles, cooked right through, a flat stone weighing down the pot lid.

name: 围祠营
The Siege Camp
before: 碎石滩上，赏金客剩下的人马全聚到了一处，扎了一座大营，营里关着十几个放牦牛的老汉，都是左手少根指头的、长得有几分像画像的、或者只是不肯回话的。赏金客说一个个审，审出霍山为止。营外的雪地上，蹄印一直通向碎石滩最深处的那座山神祠。

On the gravel flats all the bounty hunters' remaining men have gathered into one great camp, and inside it a dozen old yak herders are held: ones missing a finger on the left hand, ones who look a little like the portrait, or ones who simply wouldn't answer. The hunters say they'll question every one until they find Huo Shan. Outside the camp, the tracks in the snow lead on towards the Mountain God's shrine at the very heart of the flats.
after: 大营被打破了，老汉们一个个放了出来，可里头没有老石头。一个老汉悄悄说，老石头前天就看出来不对，赶着牛往山神祠去了，「他说，甲还在祠里，他得守着」。赏金客的头领带着最后一拨人，也朝山神祠追了下去。

The camp is broken and the old men let out one by one, but Old Stone is not among them. One of them whispers that Old Stone saw trouble coming two days ago and drove his yaks towards the shrine: 'He said the armour's still in the shrine and he has to guard it.' The hunters' leader has gone after him with the last of his men.

name: 收名客
The Name Buyer
before: 碎石滩上一顶破帐篷，住着个收名字的怪老头，雇了一伙弓手看门。卖给他一个名字，他给一袋盐；名字卖了，再有人喊你，你就听不见，也不会回头。逃兵最爱来卖，卖了名字，官府就点不着他们了。老头床底下有一只口袋，鼓鼓囊囊，塞满了写着名字的布条。

In a ragged tent on the gravel flats lives a strange old man who buys names, with a band of archers to guard his door. Sell him your name and he gives you a bag of salt; after that, when someone calls it, you don't hear and don't turn round. Deserters love to sell, since then the officials can never call them up. Under his bed is a sack, stuffed fat with strips of cloth each bearing a name.
after: 弓手被赶走，老头抱着口袋说，名字只能拿名字换回去。老兵们报上各自的外号，把本名一个个换了回来。有个老兵听见同伴喊了一声他的本名，愣了好久才回头，眼泪就下来了。老头说营将也来过，没卖，只问：「能不能替别人赎？」

The archers are driven off, and the old man clutches his sack: a name can only be bought back with a name. The old soldiers give him their nicknames and take back their real names one by one. One of them hears his comrade call him by his true name, and is a long time turning round, tears running. The commander came here too, the old man says. He didn't sell. He only asked: 'Can I buy back other people's?'

name: 代书摊
The Letter-Writer's Stall
before: 碎石滩边上一个代写家书的摊子，招牌写着「寄书过山，十日必达」。几个刀手守着摊子，摊主收了钱，信就往身后的箱子里一扔。你们拿着那封「寄凉州」的信去问路，摊主一看封口的火漆，脸就白了，叫刀手把信抢下来。

At the edge of the gravel flats is a stall that writes letters home, with a sign: LETTERS OVER THE MOUNTAIN, TEN DAYS GUARANTEED. A few swordsmen guard it, and once the stallholder has his money he tosses the letter into the chest behind him. You bring him the letter for Liangzhou to ask the way, and when he sees the wax seal he goes white and tells his swordsmen to snatch it.
after: 刀手被打散，箱子里倒出来几百封没寄的信。摊主跪着说山封了十年，信根本过不去，他只是收钱。他认得那块火漆：「是营将的私印。十年前他来问过，信能不能寄，我说能。后来他又来，把信要了回去，说不用寄了。」他想不通，信怎么又落到了驿袋里。

The swordsmen are scattered and the chest spills out hundreds of unsent letters. The stallholder kneels and confesses: the mountain has been closed ten years, no letter can get over, he just takes the money. He knows that wax: 'It's the commander's private seal. Ten years ago he came to ask if a letter could be sent, and I said yes. Later he came back and took it away again, said there was no need to send it.' He can't think how it ended up in the mailbag.

name: 甲片摊
The Armour-Scale Stall
before: 碎石滩上一伙卖护身符的，摊上摆着一片片生锈的铁甲叶，说是从山神祠里那副「神甲」上掰下来的，戴一片，雪崩埋不着。几个刀手吆喝着拦人买，一片要一头羊。转山的老人们排着队掏钱，生怕晚了买不着。

On the gravel flats a gang is selling amulets: rusty iron armour scales laid out in rows, said to have been broken off the 'god's armour' in the Mountain God's shrine. Wear one and no avalanche can bury you. A few swordsmen bawl and block the way so people will buy, one sheep a scale, and old pilgrims queue up with their money, afraid of missing out.
after: 刀手被打跑了。老甲匠拿起一片看了看就扔了：「这是马掌铁剪的，我的甲叶，片片有记号。」他说祠里那副甲一片也没少过，「有人每个月去擦，擦得锃亮」。老人们把羊牵了回去，有个老阿妈还是揣走了一片，说灵不灵的，图个心安。

The swordsmen are chased off. The old armourer picks up a scale, looks at it and throws it away: 'Cut from horseshoe iron. Every scale I made has my mark.' Not one scale is missing from the armour in the shrine, he says: 'Someone polishes it every month till it shines.' The old pilgrims lead their sheep home, though one old woman keeps a scale anyway. Whether it works or not, she says, it eases the heart.

name: 祠前坡
Shrine Slope
before: 碎石滩深处一道缓坡，坡顶就是山神祠。赏金客的头领带着最后一拨牦牛骑堵在坡下，坡上隐约有一头牦牛，一个人，坐在祠门口不动。头领吹着口哨，让手下排成一排往上冲：「三百两，就在上头。」

Deep in the gravel flats a gentle slope rises, and at its top stands the Mountain God's shrine. The bounty hunters' leader has the last of his yak riders drawn up across the foot of it. Up on the slope you can just make out one yak and one man, sitting motionless at the shrine door. The leader whistles and lines his men up to charge: 'Three hundred taels, right up there.'
after: 牦牛骑被打散，头领被你们捆了，海捕文书撕成了碎片。副将带着老兵们走上来，在坡下排成了一排，谁也没往上走。坡顶那个人还坐在祠门口，看了你们很久，才慢慢站起来，转身进了祠。

The yak riders are scattered, their leader tied up and the warrant torn to shreds. The lieutenant comes up with the old soldiers and they form a line at the foot of the slope, and none of them goes further. The man at the top still sits at the shrine door. He watches you a long time, then slowly gets up, turns, and goes into the shrine.

name: 老石头圈
Old Stone's Fold
before: 山脚下一圈牛粪垒的矮墙，墙里是老石头过冬的牛圈和一间石屋。赏金客走之前留了几个刀手在这里蹲守，把老石头的牛全宰了吃，石屋里的东西扔了一地，正在拿他的被褥烤火。

At the mountain's foot is a low wall of dried dung enclosing Old Stone's winter fold and a stone hut. Before they left, the bounty hunters posted a few swordsmen here to lie in wait. They have slaughtered and eaten Old Stone's cattle, thrown everything in the hut on the floor, and are burning his bedding to keep warm.
after: 刀手被赶走了。石屋收拾干净，墙上挂着一只汉人的茶碗，炕上的被子被老兵们叠成了方方正正的一块。副将摸着叠好的被子说，营里只有一个人叠被子叠得这么方，「十二年，天天这么叠」。

The swordsmen are driven out. You tidy the hut: a Han teacup hangs on the wall, and the old soldiers fold the quilt on the bed into a perfect square block. Running his hand over it, the lieutenant says only one man in the camp ever folded a quilt that square: 'Twelve years, every single day.'
first: 刀手们来不及带走的东西：两腔吃剩的牦牛肉、一皮袋青稞酒、一捆抢来的皮绳、几张赏金客的通缉画像，还有老石头的一只奶桶，被他们拿来装了马料。

What the swordsmen couldn't carry off: two half-eaten yak carcasses, a skin of barley beer, a bundle of stolen leather rope, a few of the hunters' wanted posters, and Old Stone's milk pail, which they had been using for horse feed.
pass: 每次路过，放牛娃都替老石头守着圈，见你们来，就从石屋里捧出一桶刚挤的牦牛奶，冒着热气：「老石头交代的，当兵的来了要给喝饱。」

Every time you pass, the herd boy is minding the fold for Old Stone, and he brings out a pail of fresh yak milk from the hut, still steaming: 'Old Stone said, when soldiers come, let them drink their fill.'

name: 断邮驿
The Dead Post Station
before: 野地上一座军驿，马棚、灶房、一间收信的小屋，十年没来过一匹驿马。一伙雪山弓手占了驿站，把这里当成了抢劫过路人的据点，驿卒被他们赶去喂马。老驿卒每天还是照样把驿门擦一遍，在门口挂起一盏灯，说驿站不能没有灯。

Out in the open stands an army post station, with stables, a kitchen and a little room for receiving letters, and not one post horse has come in ten years. A band of snow-mountain archers has made it their base for robbing travellers and set the old postman to feeding their horses. Every day he still wipes down the station gate and hangs a lamp in the doorway. A station can't be without its lamp, he says.
after: 弓手被打跑，驿站收拾了出来。老驿卒捧着那封「寄凉州」的信，说他认得：十年前营将从代书摊要回这封信，是交给他保管的，后来驿袋被马贼劫走，信就丢了。「营将每个月来一趟，不问信，只问山开了没有。」他把信还给你们：「他要是不收，你们就交给秦婶。」

The archers are chased off and the station set to rights. The old postman holds the letter for Liangzhou and says he knows it. Ten years ago the commander took it back from the letter-writer and gave it to him to keep; later horse thieves stole the mailbag and the letter was lost. 'The commander comes once a month. He never asks about the letter. He only asks if the mountain is open yet.' He gives it back to you: 'If he won't take it, give it to Aunt Qin.'
first: 弓手们囤在驿站里的：一车劫来的砖茶、两袋糌粑、一副驿马的鞍子、一摞没人认领的包裹，老驿卒挨个登了簿，说等山开了一样样送出去。

The archers' hoard in the station: a cartload of looted brick tea, two bags of tsampa, a post horse's saddle, and a stack of unclaimed parcels. The old postman logs every one in his book and says he'll deliver them all once the mountain opens.
pass: 每次路过，老驿卒都在驿门口等着，灯已经点上了，灶上煨着一壶酥油茶。他照驿站的老规矩给你们验过路条，盖一个红印：「驿站有灯，路就不算断。」

Every time you pass, the old postman is waiting at the station gate with the lamp already lit and a pot of butter tea warming on the stove. He checks your passes by the old station rules and stamps them red: 'While the station has a lamp, the road isn't broken.'

name: 山神祠
The Mountain God's Shrine
before: 碎石滩最深处一座小小的石祠，祠里没有神像，只有一副明光甲挂在木架上，七百片甲叶擦得锃亮，护心镜照得见人影，头盔端端正正扣在架顶。祠门口，十几个拜甲的牧人骑在牦牛上，举着赶牛的长鞭，不许外人走近他们的「神甲」。祠里那个老汉背对着门，正拿一块旧毡擦甲。

At the very heart of the gravel flats stands a small stone shrine. There is no god's image inside, only a suit of bright plate armour hung on a wooden frame, its seven hundred scales polished till they gleam, the heart-mirror clear enough to see your face in, the helmet set squarely on top. At the door a dozen herders who worship the armour sit on their yaks with long whips raised, letting no outsider near their 'god's armour'. Inside, an old man stands with his back to the door, polishing it with an old piece of felt.
after:
拜甲的牧人退开了。老汉转过身，左手少一根小指。你们把那封信递给他，他看了看封口，没拆，揣进了怀里：「本来要写『腊月廿五回家』，不回了，就没寄。」秦婶就在屯田坝割了十年麦，他每年去帮着割，一直没敢认。

他摘下头盔，从盔里取出一块铜令，刻着「碎石营营将」：「拿去。到兵营里喊一声『碎石营，归营』，老兄弟们会来的。」那年腊月，背匣子的汉人跟他说：「山我替你守，山下你替我守。」他守了十年。如今你们来了，他要回屯田坝，帮秦婶割麦去了。

The armour's worshippers draw back. The old man turns round. His left hand is missing its little finger. You hand him the letter. He looks at the seal, doesn't open it, and tucks it inside his coat: 'It was going to say I'd be home on the twenty-fifth of the twelfth month. I didn't go, so I didn't send it.' Aunt Qin has been reaping barley on the terraces for ten years, and every year he has gone to help, and never dared tell her who he is.

He lifts down the helmet and takes from inside it a bronze token engraved COMMANDER, GRAVEL CAMP: 'Take it. Go into a barracks and call out Gravel Camp, fall in!, and the old lads will come.' That twelfth month, the Han man with the casket told him: 'I'll guard the mountain for you. You guard the foot of it for me.' He has, for ten years. Now that you've come, he's going back to the terraces to help Aunt Qin with the harvest.
